name: Diaphragmatic breathing (360)
cues: Seated or side-lying. Hands on lower ribs. Inhale wide into ribs and back, not just belly. Exhale slow through pursed lips.
modifications: Side-lying with a pillow between knees if seated is uncomfortable.
source_ref: judgment - no constraint governs; review
benefit: Teaches your ribs and diaphragm to move together, which is what lets the pelvic floor relax and contract properly. Almost everything else here works better once this does.
open_questions: Any preference on breath cues you use with patients?

name: Pelvic floor activation
cues: Exhale, gently lift as if stopping gas. Hold 3-5s. Fully release. Release is as important as the lift.
modifications: Reduce hold to 2s. Do seated if lying is uncomfortable.
source_ref: SOGC/CSEP 2019 Rec 5 - PFMT daily; technique instruction recommended
benefit: Regular pelvic floor training during pregnancy cuts the odds of urinary leaking roughly in half now, and by about a third after birth.
open_questions: Can you refer us to a pelvic floor PT? Guideline says technique instruction matters.

name: Pelvic floor relaxation / down-training
cues: Supported deep squat or side-lying. Long slow exhale, let the pelvic floor soften and drop. No lifting.
modifications: Seated on a chair, knees wide, forward lean on forearms.
source_ref: SOGC/CSEP 2019 Rec 5 - PFMT daily; technique instruction recommended
benefit: Your pelvic floor needs to let go as well as squeeze. Practising the release now builds a skill that matters for delivery and for everyday comfort.
open_questions: Worth introducing this in T1 or is it a T3 thing?

name: Pelvic floor quick flicks
cues: Fast light lifts, 1s on 1s off, 10 reps. Trains the fast-twitch response for cough and sneeze.
modifications: Halve the reps. Stop if you lose the sense of release between reps.
source_ref: SOGC/CSEP 2019 Rec 5 - PFMT daily; technique instruction recommended
benefit: Trains the fast response that stops leaking when you cough, sneeze, or laugh. Different skill from the long hold, and it needs its own practice.

name: Side-lying supported breathing
cues: Left side, pillow between knees and under bump as it grows. Slow nasal inhale, longer exhale. 5 min.
modifications: Add a pillow under the ribs if the shoulder aches.
source_ref: judgment - no constraint governs; review
benefit: Down-regulates a nervous system that's working hard. Counts as a real session on the days when nothing else does.

name: Cat-cow
cues: Quadruped. Inhale to arch gently, exhale to round. Small range. Stop if the belly cones or tents.
modifications: Do it seated or standing with hands on thighs if the wrists or knees complain.
source_ref: SOGC/CSEP 2019 impl. - diastasis: avoid abdominal curls
benefit: Keeps the spine moving as posture shifts. Also the easiest place to notice belly coning early, while it's still simple to work around.

name: Seated thoracic rotation
cues: Sit tall, hands crossed on chest. Rotate from the ribs, not the low back. 8 each side, slow.
modifications: Reduce range. Keep hips square throughout.
source_ref: SOGC/CSEP 2019 Rec 4 - yoga/gentle stretching additive
benefit: Rotation through the mid-back gets stiff as the ribcage widens. Keeping it mobile takes load off the low back.
open_questions: feel like adding reeasons as to why this is beneficial or what is preepping theem for is iimportant. Video resource miht be nice heere too

name: Half-kneeling hip flexor stretch
cues: Half-kneel, tuck the pelvis under, shift weight forward slightly. Hold 30s. Should feel front-of-hip, not low back.
modifications: Hold a chair for balance. Pad the down knee.
source_ref: SOGC/CSEP 2019 Rec 4 - yoga/gentle stretching additive
benefit: Hip flexors shorten as the pelvis tilts forward through pregnancy, and that's a common source of low back ache. Opening them helps directly.

name: Ankle and calf mobility
cues: Hands on wall, knee travels forward over toes without the heel lifting. 10 each side.
modifications: Seated ankle circles if standing is uncomfortable.
source_ref: judgment - no constraint governs; review
benefit: Calf pumping moves fluid out of the lower legs, which is where swelling collects. Also protects the ankles as balance shifts.
open_questions: Feel like adding reeasons as to why this is beneficial or what is preepping theem for is iimportant

name: Wide-knee child's pose
cues: Knees wide so there's room for the bump. Sit hips back toward heels, arms long. Breathe into the back ribs.
modifications: Sit back on a cushion, or do it standing folded over a counter.
source_ref: SOGC/CSEP 2019 Rec 4 - yoga/gentle stretching additive
benefit: Opens the hips and lets the low back decompress. One of the few positions that stays comfortable most of the way through.

name: Brisk walk
cues: Pace where you can talk but not sing. 20-30 min. Water before, during, after.
modifications: Shorten to 10 min. Split into two walks. Move indoors if it's hot or humid.
source_ref: SOGC/CSEP 2019 Rec 2 - talk test / SOGC/CSEP 2019 Box 1 - avoid excessive heat/humidity; hydrate
benefit: The single most studied activity in pregnancy. Reduces the odds of gestational diabetes, pre-eclampsia, and high blood pressure. No equipment, no learning curve.
open_questions: Any pace or duration ceiling for Alex specifically?

name: Easy recovery walk
cues: Conversational, unhurried. 10-15 min. This counts. It is not a lesser option.
modifications: Five minutes is a complete session on a hard day.
source_ref: SOGC/CSEP 2019 Rec 2 - talk test
benefit: Movement below your usual effort still counts. Walking is linked to lower odds of developing abdominal separation, which makes easy days genuinely productive.

name: Box squat
cues: Feet hip-width or wider. Sit back to a chair, tap, stand. Exhale on the way up. 8-12.
modifications: Raise the chair height. Hold a doorframe for support.
source_ref: SOGC/CSEP 2019 Rec 4 - aerobic + resistance, high-quality evidence
benefit: Builds the legs and glutes you'll use for every stand-up, stair, and eventually every pick-up of a car seat. The box means you can always regress it.

name: Wall push-up
cues: Hands on wall shoulder-height. Body in one line. Lower with control, press away. 10-15.
modifications: Step closer to the wall to make it easier. Incline on a counter to make it harder.
source_ref: SOGC/CSEP 2019 Rec 4 - aerobic + resistance, high-quality evidence
benefit: Upper body strength without lying down or loading the belly. Scales in both directions just by moving your feet.
open_questions: add in normal push uo as an option? For earlier stages?

name: Bird dog
cues: Quadruped. Extend opposite arm and leg, keep hips level. 5 each side. Stop if the belly cones.
modifications: Extend only the leg, or only the arm. Reduce the range.
source_ref: SOGC/CSEP 2019 impl. - diastasis: avoid abdominal curls
benefit: Trains deep core control without curling the spine, which is the kind of core work that stays appropriate as the belly grows.
open_questions: Is quadruped core work fine to continue as she progresses?

name: Glute bridge
cues: On the back, feet flat. Exhale, press through heels, lift hips. Lower slowly. 10-12.
modifications: If you feel light-headed, nauseous or unwell on your back, switch to the side-lying clamshell.
source_ref: SOGC/CSEP 2019 Rec 6 - supine is SYMPTOM-triggered, not calendar
benefit: Strong glutes carry load the low back would otherwise take. One of the highest-value movements for pregnancy back pain.
open_questions: Guideline says supine is symptom-triggered, not week-based. Agree?

name: Side-lying clamshell
cues: On your side, knees bent and stacked. Lift the top knee without rolling the hips back. 12 each side.
modifications: Add a band above the knees to progress. Reduce range if the hip pinches.
source_ref: SOGC/CSEP 2019 Rec 4 - aerobic + resistance, high-quality evidence
benefit: Targets the side glutes that stabilise the pelvis. Directly relevant to the hip and pelvic girdle pain that often shows up later.

name: Seated band row
cues: Band anchored ahead. Sit tall, pull elbows back past the ribs, squeeze. Exhale on the pull. 10-12.
modifications: Loop the band around a doorknob. Use a lighter band.
source_ref: SOGC/CSEP 2019 Rec 4 - aerobic + resistance, high-quality evidence
benefit: Counteracts the forward pull on the shoulders as the chest changes. Upper back strength is what keeps posture from collapsing.

name: Suitcase carry
cues: One weight, one hand. Walk tall, resist the lean. 20-30s per side. Keep breathing - do not hold your breath.
modifications: Go lighter. Stand still and hold rather than walking.
source_ref: SOGC/CSEP 2019 impl. - avoid breath-hold if light-headed w/ Valsalva
benefit: Trains the core to resist being pulled sideways, which is exactly what carrying a baby on one hip demands. Practical strength.

name: Warm-up and cool-down
cues: Include both in every session. Ligaments loosen in pregnancy, which changes range of motion and raises injury risk.
modifications: Five minutes of easy walking counts as either.
source_ref: SOGC/CSEP 2019 impl. - ligament laxity, warm-up/cool-down suggested
benefit: Pregnancy hormones loosen ligaments, so joints move further than they used to and injury risk goes up. A few easy minutes at each end is genuine protection.

name: Incline push-up
cues: Hands on a counter or bench. Body in one line, lower with control, press away. 8-12.
modifications: Use a higher surface to make it easier, lower to make it harder.
source_ref: SOGC/CSEP 2019 Rec 4 - aerobic + resistance, high-quality evidence
benefit: The middle rung between wall and floor. Lets you keep progressing the same pattern instead of being stuck at one difficulty for nine months.
open_questions: Approved 8/5 — read cues before seeding

name: Push-up (floor)
cues: Hands under shoulders, body in one line. Lower with control. Stop if the belly cones. From knees is a full version, not a lesser one.
modifications: Drop to knees. Move to incline once lying face-down stops being comfortable.
source_ref: SOGC/CSEP 2019 Rec 4 - aerobic + resistance, high-quality evidence
benefit: The hardest rung of the same pattern. Face-down gets impractical as the bump grows, so this one falls out of the pool on its own and the incline takes over.
open_questions: Approved 8/5 — read cues before seeding

name: Goblet squat
cues: Hold one dumbbell at your chest. Feet a little wider than hips. Sit down between your hips, chest tall. Exhale on the way up. Do not hold your breath at any point. 8-12 reps.
modifications: Go lighter, or sit back to a chair or box. Reduce depth as the bump grows - a shallower squat is still a squat.
source_ref: Duchette 2024 IJWH review of prenatal RT - RT safe/beneficial; balance caution grows with gestation. Petrov Fieril 2015 RCT (Acta Obstet Gynecol Scand) - squats retained, made less deep
benefit: The squat is the single most transferable movement in pregnancy - it is how you get off the floor, off the toilet, and out of a chair for the next nine months. Holding the weight at your chest actually helps balance rather than hurting it.
open_questions: Capped at t3_early on balance grounds - confirm with OB whether to extend

name: Dumbbell Romanian deadlift
cues: Dumbbells in front of your thighs. Push your hips back, keep a long spine, lower until you feel your hamstrings. Stand tall by squeezing your glutes. Exhale on the way up. 8-12 reps.
modifications: Shorten the range. Go lighter. Widen your stance as the bump grows.
source_ref: Duchette 2024 IJWH review of prenatal RT - RT improves posture, lumbar lordosis, back pain. SOGC/CSEP 2019 Rec 4 - aerobic + resistance, high-quality evidence
benefit: Around three in four pregnant women get back pain. Strong glutes and hamstrings take load off the low back, and this is the most direct way to build them. Bilateral and stable - no balance demand.

name: Supported split squat
cues: One foot forward, one back. Hold a chair or wall with one hand. Lower straight down, back knee toward the floor. 8-10 each side.
modifications: Reduce depth. Hold with both hands. Drop to a static hold if the movement feels unsteady.
source_ref: Duchette 2024 IJWH review of prenatal RT - lunges rely on balance, less safe as centre of gravity shifts; support mitigates
benefit: Single-leg strength is what keeps stairs, curbs and getting out of the car easy in the third trimester. The hand support is not a downgrade - it is what makes this appropriate to keep doing while pregnant.
open_questions: Capped at t2_late on balance grounds

name: Low step-up
cues: Use a low, stable step. Step up under control, step down under control. Do not push off the bottom foot. 8-10 each side.
modifications: Lower the step height. Hold a wall or rail. Reduce reps.
source_ref: Duchette 2024 IJWH review of prenatal RT - balance-dependent movements need caution as gestation advances
benefit: Direct practice for stairs and curbs, which get harder as your centre of gravity moves forward. Builds the same pattern you use dozens of times a day.
open_questions: Capped at t2_late on balance grounds

name: Heel raise
cues: Hand on a wall for balance. Rise onto the balls of your feet, pause, lower slowly. 12-15 reps.
modifications: Hold with both hands. Do it seated if standing is uncomfortable.
source_ref: Petrov Fieril 2015 RCT (Acta Obstet Gynecol Scand) - the specific substitution used in place of squat jumps in the prenatal RCT protocol
benefit: Calf work pumps fluid out of the lower legs, which is where swelling collects. This is the exact movement used as the safe substitute in a prenatal resistance training trial.

name: Seated dumbbell shoulder press
cues: Sit tall on a bench or chair, back supported. Press the dumbbells overhead without arching your low back. Exhale as you press. 8-12 reps.
modifications: Go lighter. Press one arm at a time. Reduce range if your shoulders feel tight.
source_ref: Duchette 2024 IJWH review of prenatal RT - upright position, no supine concern. SOGC/CSEP 2019 Rec 4 - aerobic + resistance, high-quality evidence
benefit: Upright pressing stays available the whole way through - no bump in the way, no lying on your back. You will use this strength every time you lift a car seat.

name: Incline dumbbell press
cues: Set the bench to an incline - roughly 45 degrees or higher. Press the dumbbells up, lower with control. 8-12 reps.
modifications: Raise the incline further as pregnancy progresses. Go lighter. Switch to a seated press if it stops feeling good.
source_ref: Duchette 2024 IJWH review of prenatal RT - inclined bench named as the specific modification for supine pressing
benefit: This is the pressing movement that survives all three trimesters. The incline is not a compromise - it is the named modification that keeps you off your back while still training the same muscles.
open_questions: Confirm minimum incline angle with OB or PT

name: Single-arm dumbbell row
cues: One hand and knee on a bench, flat back. Pull the dumbbell toward your hip, elbow close. Exhale on the pull. 8-12 each side.
modifications: Stand and brace on a chair instead of kneeling on a bench. Go lighter.
source_ref: Duchette 2024 IJWH review of prenatal RT - RT improves posture and lumbar lordosis. SOGC/CSEP 2019 Rec 4 - aerobic + resistance, high-quality evidence
benefit: Your chest gets heavier and your shoulders get pulled forward. Rowing is the direct counter, and upper back strength is what stops posture collapsing as the pregnancy goes on.

name: Band pull-apart
cues: Hold a band at shoulder height, arms straight. Pull it apart until it touches your chest, squeeze your shoulder blades, return slowly. 12-15 reps.
modifications: Widen your grip to make it easier. Use a lighter band.
source_ref: Duchette 2024 IJWH review of prenatal RT - bands named as a safe alternative to free weights. SOGC/CSEP 2019 Rec 4 - aerobic + resistance, high-quality evidence
benefit: Low-effort, high-value postural work you can do anywhere. Bands are specifically named as a safe alternative when a dropped weight would be a concern.

name: Farmer carry
cues: A dumbbell in each hand, arms at your sides. Walk tall for 20-40 seconds. Keep breathing throughout - do not hold your breath.
modifications: Go lighter. Stand and hold rather than walking. Shorten the time.
source_ref: Duchette 2024 IJWH review of prenatal RT - avoid Valsalva; breathing cue is the control. SOGC/CSEP 2019 Rec 4 - aerobic + resistance, high-quality evidence
benefit: Loaded carries build the whole trunk without any crunching or lying down. Practical strength for carrying a baby, a car seat, and groceries at the same time.

name: Incline walk
cues: Treadmill incline or a hill. Pace where you can talk but not sing. 15-25 min. Water before, during and after.
modifications: Reduce the incline. Shorten the time. Move indoors if it is hot or humid.
source_ref: SOGC/CSEP 2019 Rec 4 - aerobic + resistance, high-quality evidence - 150 min/wk moderate, talk test. Duchette 2024 IJWH review of prenatal RT - RT + aerobic together best outcomes
benefit: Real conditioning without impact or fall risk. Combining aerobic work with strength produces better outcomes than either alone - this is the aerobic half.

name: Stationary bike
cues: Sit upright rather than leaning forward over the bars. Conversational effort. 15-30 min.
modifications: Reduce resistance. Shorten the time. Raise the handlebars so you can stay upright.
source_ref: SOGC/CSEP 2019 Rec 4 - aerobic + resistance, high-quality evidence - stationary cycling named as a safer alternative. Petrov Fieril 2015 RCT (Acta Obstet Gynecol Scand) - forward-leaning cycling loads the pelvic floor
benefit: Named in the guideline as a safe alternative to outdoor cycling. No fall risk, no impact, and you control the effort exactly. Staying upright keeps load off the pelvic floor.
open_questions: Equipment vocab has no 'bike' value - see note

name: Dumbbell biceps curl
cues: Stand tall, elbows at your sides. Curl without swinging. Exhale on the way up. 10-15 reps.
modifications: Go lighter. Sit down to remove any temptation to use your body for momentum.
source_ref: Duchette 2024 IJWH review of prenatal RT - upright/seated position, no supine concern
benefit: Small, low-risk, and it stays available the whole way through. Arm strength is what you use lifting a car seat in and out of a base a dozen times a day.

name: Dumbbell lateral raise
cues: Light dumbbells at your sides. Lift out to shoulder height with soft elbows, lower slowly. 12-15 reps.
modifications: Go lighter - this one is almost always lighter than people expect. Raise to half height.
source_ref: Duchette 2024 IJWH review of prenatal RT - upright/seated position, no supine concern
benefit: Shoulder strength without pressing overhead. Useful on days when the bump makes bigger movements awkward but you still want to train.

name: Dumbbell sumo squat
cues: Wide stance, toes turned out, one dumbbell held in both hands in front. Sit straight down between your hips. Exhale on the way up. 10-15 reps.
modifications: Go lighter, or hold no weight at all. Reduce depth as the bump grows.
source_ref: Duchette 2024 IJWH review of prenatal RT - balance caution advances with gestation
benefit: The wide stance gives the bump somewhere to go, which makes this squat more comfortable than a narrow one as pregnancy progresses. Same leg and glute work, better fit.
open_questions: Capped at t3_early - the dumbbell has nowhere to go late. Consider goblet position instead.

name: Cable triceps pushdown
cues: Stand tall facing the stack, elbows pinned at your sides. Push down until your arms are straight, return under control. 12-15 reps.
modifications: Go lighter. Step back slightly if the cable pulls you forward.
source_ref: Duchette 2024 IJWH review of prenatal RT - upright/seated position, no supine concern
benefit: Upright, stable, and easy to load exactly as light as you want. The cable keeps tension even at the top, so it does not need much weight to be worthwhile.

name: Standing cable fly
cues: Cables set at chest height, one in each hand. Stand in a small split stance and bring your hands together in front of your chest. Exhale as you close. 10-15 reps.
modifications: Go lighter. Narrow the range. Do one arm at a time if the split stance feels unstable.
source_ref: Duchette 2024 IJWH review of prenatal RT - standing variation avoids the supine bench position entirely
benefit: Chest work with no bench and no lying down, so it stays available through all three trimesters. Standing also means you can step out of it instantly if anything feels off.
open_questions: STANDING only - a bench fly is supine and is deliberately not in the library

name: Cable face pull
cues: Rope attachment at face height. Pull toward your forehead, elbows high, squeezing your shoulder blades. 12-15 reps.
modifications: Go lighter. Sit on a bench facing the stack if standing gets tiring.
source_ref: Duchette 2024 IJWH review of prenatal RT - RT improves posture and lumbar lordosis
benefit: Your chest gets heavier and your shoulders get pulled forward. This is the most direct counter there is, and it is nearly impossible to do badly with a light weight.

name: Seated low cable row
cues: Seated, feet on the platform, long spine. Pull the handle to your stomach, elbows close. Exhale on the pull. 10-15 reps.
modifications: Go lighter. Widen your knees to give the bump room as it grows.
source_ref: judgment - machines/cables remove the balance and stabilisation demand the literature cautions about for free weights as gestation advances (Duchette 2024 IJWH review of prenatal RT)
benefit: Seated and supported, so it stays comfortable long after free-weight rowing gets awkward. Upper back strength is what keeps posture from collapsing later on.

name: Standing cable pullover
cues: Rope or bar high on the stack. Stand tall, arms long, pull down in an arc to your thighs without bending your elbows. 12-15 reps.
modifications: Go lighter. Kneel on one knee if standing feels unsteady.
source_ref: Duchette 2024 IJWH review of prenatal RT - standing variation avoids the supine bench position
benefit: Lat work without an overhead pull or a bench. Good on days when reaching overhead does not feel great but you still want to train your back.

name: Cable glute kickback
cues: Ankle cuff on one leg, hold the frame with both hands. Drive the leg back and squeeze. 12-15 each side.
modifications: Hold on with both hands throughout. Reduce range. Swap to a side-lying clamshell if balance feels off.
source_ref: Duchette 2024 IJWH review of prenatal RT - single-leg stance is balance-dependent, caution advances with gestation
benefit: Loaded glute work that isolates one side at a time. Strong glutes take load off the low back, which is where most pregnancy pain shows up.
open_questions: Capped at t2_late on balance grounds - single-leg stance

name: Lat pulldown
cues: Seated, thighs under the pads. Pull the bar to your collarbone with a tall spine - do not lean back to move more weight. Exhale on the pull. 10-15 reps.
modifications: Go lighter. Use a neutral grip if your shoulders prefer it.
source_ref: judgment - machines/cables remove the balance and stabilisation demand the literature cautions about for free weights as gestation advances (Duchette 2024 IJWH review of prenatal RT)
benefit: One of the best back exercises that stays available all the way through, because you are seated and braced the entire time.

name: Leg extension
cues: Seated, back against the pad. Straighten your knees under control, lower slowly. 12-15 reps.
modifications: Go lighter. Reduce the range. Adjust the seat back as the bump grows.
source_ref: judgment - machines/cables remove the balance and stabilisation demand the literature cautions about for free weights as gestation advances (Duchette 2024 IJWH review of prenatal RT)
benefit: Loaded leg work with zero balance demand and nothing to hold. When squatting starts to feel awkward later on, this keeps your quads working.

name: Seated hamstring curl
cues: Seated, pad above your ankles. Curl your heels down and under, return slowly. 12-15 reps.
modifications: Go lighter. Reduce the range.
source_ref: judgment - machines/cables remove the balance and stabilisation demand the literature cautions about for free weights as gestation advances (Duchette 2024 IJWH review of prenatal RT)
benefit: Hamstring strength supports the pelvis and low back, and the seated machine version needs no balance at all. Pairs with the leg extension for a full lower-body session on a hard day.

name: Assisted pull-up
cues: Set the assistance high enough that you can do all your reps with control. Pull with your back, not your arms. Exhale on the pull. 6-10 reps.
modifications: Add more assistance. Fewer reps. Switch to a lat pulldown if stepping onto the platform feels awkward.
source_ref: judgment - machines/cables remove the balance and stabilisation demand the literature cautions about for free weights as gestation advances (Duchette 2024 IJWH review of prenatal RT)
benefit: The assistance dial means you control the load precisely, and can keep dialling it up as pregnancy progresses rather than dropping the movement.

name: Chest press machine
cues: Seated upright, back on the pad. Press forward and return under control. Exhale as you press. 10-15 reps.
modifications: Go lighter. Adjust the seat so the handles start at chest height, not behind you.
source_ref: Duchette 2024 IJWH review of prenatal RT - upright seated press avoids the supine position entirely
benefit: The pressing movement that survives the whole pregnancy. Upright, supported, and there is no bump in the way - which is more than you can say for a bench press.

name: Shoulder press machine
cues: Seated, back against the pad. Press overhead without arching your low back. Exhale as you press. 10-15 reps.
modifications: Go lighter. Press one arm at a time. Skip it if reaching overhead is uncomfortable.
source_ref: judgment - machines/cables remove the balance and stabilisation demand the literature cautions about for free weights as gestation advances (Duchette 2024 IJWH review of prenatal RT)
benefit: Same benefit as the dumbbell version with a back rest, which matters more as the low back takes on more work.

name: Seated hip abduction
cues: Seated, pads on the outside of your knees. Push out, squeeze, return slowly. 12-15 reps.
modifications: Go lighter. Reduce the range. Swap to a side-lying clamshell if the seat is uncomfortable.
source_ref: judgment - machines/cables remove the balance and stabilisation demand the literature cautions about for free weights as gestation advances (Duchette 2024 IJWH review of prenatal RT)
benefit: This is the loaded version of the clamshell. The side glutes stabilise your pelvis, and this is one of the few ways to actually load them - directly relevant to the hip and pelvic pain that often shows up later.
